previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of diastolic heart failure, chronic anticoagulation, and prior GI bleed presented with headache, chest pain, and acute anemia with a hemoglobin drop from 39 to 24.9. She was found to have a slightly elevated INR of 3.2 on Coumadin, but was hemodynamically stable. She received two units of packed red blood cells and was started on IV proton pump inhibitor therapy. Endoscopy revealed esophagitis and gastritis without active bleeding, and colonoscopy showed diverticulosis without active bleeding. Her hypoxia was attributed to mild pulmonary edema, managed with IV and oral diuretics. Her chronic chest pain persisted but was deemed non-cardiac, and headache improved without intervention. Coumadin was held initially and restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with home health services on optimized heart failure and GI protective medications, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs and monitor for rebleeding.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with a history of blood clots and now with
pleuritic left-sided chest pain unlike her prior chronic pain.

STUDY:  Chest CTA; coronal and sagittal as well as right and left oblique
reformatted images were also generated and a non-contrast phase is also
performed; abdomen and pelvis with contrast; coronal and sagittal reformatted
images were also performed.

COMPARISON:  ___.  ___.

FINDINGS:

CHEST:  The visualized portion of the thyroid appears unremarkable.  There is
no hilar, mediastinal or axillary lymphadenopathy.  There is no evidence of
aortic intramural hematoma or dissection.  A small filling defect in the
descending portion of the aortic arch represents an adherent mural thrombus
(3A; 12).  The aorta is of normal caliber throughout its course in the chest. 
Pulmonary arteries show no filling defects down to subsegmental levels.  There
is no pleural or pericardial effusion.  Mild dependent bibasilar atelectasis
is noted.  There is bilateral posterior pleural thickening, stable from prior
studies and also scattered intrapulmonary blood which have not changed since
prior study.  The previously described right upper lobe nodule measures 9 x 6
mm (3A; 23) which is relatively unchanged from the prior measurements of 8 x 6
mm in ___ and was reported to be stable since ___.

ABDOMEN:  The liver shows no evidence of intrahepatic biliary dilatation.  A
small region of hypodensity around the falciform ligament is in a usual
location for focal fat.  The gallbladder is prominent but shows no evidence of
wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, cholelithiasis.  The spleen is normal
in size and appearance.  The pancreas shows no masses, cysts or
calcifications.  The adrenal glands are normal appearing bilaterally.  A
well-circumscribed hypodensity in the upper pole of the left kidney too small
to characterize likely represents a simple cyst.  The small and large
intestine show no evidence of wall thickening or obstruction.  The aorta, IVC,
portal vein and their major branches all appear patent.  No lymphadenopathy is
seen.  No free air or free fluid is noted.

PELVIS:  The bladder, uterus and rectum appear unremarkable.  Sigmoid
diverticulosis extending up into the descending and transverse colon is noted
without evidence of diverticulitis.

BONES:  Mild-to-moderate degenerative changes are noted in the thoracolumbar
spine with vacuum phenomenon at the L4-L5 as well as at the L2 and L3 and
L1-L2 intervertebral discs.  A left total hip arthroplasty is noted without
evidence of failure or loosening.

1.  No PE or acute aortic syndrome.
2.  Diverticulosis without evidence of diverticulitis.
